skill.name: create-pr
skill.description: Automates GitHub pull request preparation. It checks branches, reviews commits and changed files, generates PR text, pushes the branch, and creates the PR with GitHub CLI.
skill.summary: Prepare, push, and create GitHub pull requests from repository changes.
skill.author: Crearize

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, inline backticks, and readable Japanese documentation. The confirmed risks are the state-changing git push and gh pr create workflow, plus avoidable shell construction for the generated PR body. No prompt injection, malicious network endpoint, or obfuscated payload evidence was found.

remediation.issue: State-changing remote Git and GitHub operations
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before git push and gh pr create. Show the branch, base, title, body preview, and target repository first.

remediation.issue: PR body passed through shell command substitution
remediation.suggestion: Write the generated body to a temporary file and call gh pr create with --body-file. Avoid embedding generated text in shell syntax.
Ask the user to confirm the base branch before diffing, pushing, or creating the pull request.

content.value_statement: Pull request preparation can be slow when commits, files, tests, and issue links must be summarized. This skill reviews repository changes, drafts PR text, pushes the branch, and opens the PR with GitHub CLI.
actual_capabilities: Checks the current Git branch before creating a pull request.
Compares commits and changed files against origin/main.
Groups changed files into backend, frontend, documentation, and other areas.
Drafts a PR title, body, checklist, test summary, and related issue section.
Pushes the current branch to origin when the user proceeds.
Creates and opens a GitHub pull request with gh CLI.
limitations: Requires Git, GitHub CLI, and repository authentication to be configured.
Assumes origin/main is the correct comparison branch unless changed by the user.
Does not run QA checks itself; it expects QA to be complete before use.
Can push commits and create remote PRs, so users must review before execution.

use_cases.title: Feature Branch Submission
use_cases.description: Prepare a polished PR from a completed feature branch with summary, tests, checklist, and issue closure details.

use_cases.title: Maintenance Fix Review
use_cases.description: Turn a small fix branch into a review-ready PR with clear scope and changed file categories.

use_cases.title: Team Workflow Standardization
use_cases.description: Use a consistent PR format across backend, frontend, and documentation changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub pull request for my current branch. Show me the branch, changed files, generated title, and PR body before pushing.

prompt_templates.title: Create PR With Issue Link
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request for this branch against origin/main and link issue #123. Include the test status and a concise summary.

prompt_templates.title: Create PR With Change Categories
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the commits and changed files, group backend, frontend, and documentation changes, then draft the PR. Ask before running git push.

prompt_templates.title: Create Release-Ready PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a release-ready PR with risk notes, reviewer guidance, checklist status, and screenshots section. Use gh CLI only after I approve the preview.

output_examples.input: User asks to create a PR for a feature branch that adds profile settings.
output_examples.output: A PR title, concise summary, categorized changes, test checklist, related issue line, and a GitHub PR URL after approval.

output_examples.input: User asks for a bug fix PR linked to issue 456.
output_examples.output: The skill reports branch checks, summarizes the fix, includes test evidence, references issue 456, and creates the PR through GitHub CLI.
The skill highlights updated documents, keeps technical sections minimal, and provides a review-ready PR description.

best_practices: Review the generated title and body before approving any push or PR creation.
Run QA checks and commit all changes before starting the workflow.
Confirm the base branch, issue number, and test status with the user.
anti_patterns: Do not run the workflow from main or another protected branch.
Do not create a PR while uncommitted changes are present.
Do not paste unreviewed generated text into a public PR.

faq.question: Does this skill create the PR automatically?
faq.answer: It can create the PR through GitHub CLI after the user approves the preview and push.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: It requires Git, GitHub CLI, repository access, and an authenticated GitHub account.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill expects QA checks to be complete and records the test status in the PR body.

faq.question: Can I change the base branch?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell the assistant the target base branch before it compares changes or creates the PR.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: It can be used in private repositories, but it may push commits and send PR text to GitHub.

faq.question: What should I review before approval?
faq.answer: Review the branch name, changed files, generated title, PR body, issue link, and test claims.
